cases.expected: NumericIndicator.abs() returns a new NumericIndicator whose value at any index is the absolute value of the original delegate. For a delegate ConstantIndicator(-10), getValue(0) should be 10.
cases.description: Verify that abs() converts a purely negative constant indicator to its positive absolute value.

cases.expected: For a delegate Indicator returning [-5, 0, 7] at indices 0,1,2 respectively, NumericIndicator.abs().getValue(0) == 5, getValue(1) == 0, getValue(2) == 7.
cases.description: Check that abs() correctly handles a mix of negative, zero, and positive values.

cases.expected: When the delegate already provides only non‑negative values (e.g., ConstantIndicator(12)), abs() should return a NumericIndicator whose values are unchanged; getValue(0) == 12.
cases.description: Ensure that abs() is a no‑op for already positive values.

cases.expected: For a delegate ConstantIndicator(0), abs().getValue(0) should be 0.
cases.description: Validate that zero remains zero after applying abs().

cases.expected: Calling abs() twice yields the same result as calling it once; i.e., abs().abs().getValue(i) == abs().getValue(i) for any index i.
cases.description: Confirm idempotence of the abs() operation.

cases.expected: The original NumericIndicator instance remains unchanged after abs() is called; its delegate values are still the original (e.g., -3 at index 0).
cases.description: Verify that abs() does not mutate the original indicator but returns a new instance.

cases.expected: When the delegate returns a very large positive value (e.g., ConstantIndicator(9_223_372_036_854_775_807)), NumericIndicator.abs().getValue(0) should equal the same large value, confirming that abs() does not alter positive numbers regardless of magnitude.
cases.description: Validate that abs() correctly handles extreme positive values without overflow or modification.

cases.expected: If the delegate returns a negative zero (e.g., ConstantIndicator(-0.0)), NumericIndicator.abs().getValue(0) should be 0.0 (positive zero), confirming correct handling of signed zero.
cases.description: Check that abs() normalises negative zero to standard zero.

cases.expected: For a delegate that yields NaN (e.g., ConstantIndicator(Num.NaN)), NumericIndicator.abs().getValue(0) should also be NaN, preserving the undefined nature of the value.
cases.description: Ensure that abs() propagates NaN values unchanged.

cases.expected: The NumericIndicator returned by abs() must retain the same BarSeries as the original indicator; calling getBarSeries() on both instances should return the identical BarSeries object.
cases.description: Confirm that the series context is preserved after applying abs().

cases.expected: The delegate of the indicator returned by abs() must be a different object from the original delegate (i.e., NumericIndicator.abs().delegate() != original.delegate()), while still producing identical absolute values for all indices.
cases.description: Verify that abs() creates a new delegate wrapper rather than reusing the original, ensuring immutability of the delegate chain.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException (or NullPointerException) when creating a NumericIndicator with a null delegate before calling abs().
cases.description: Attempt to construct a NumericIndicator using NumericIndicator.of(null) and then invoke abs(); the factory should reject a null delegate and throw an exception, preventing abs() from being executed.

cases.expected: NullPointerException when the underlying delegate's getValue(index) returns null and abs() attempts to compute the absolute value.
cases.description: Create a custom Indicator implementation whose getValue method returns null. Wrap it with NumericIndicator.of(...). Calling abs().getValue(0) should trigger a NPE because UnaryOperation.abs cannot handle a null Num.

cases.expected: IndexOutOfBoundsException when the delegate throws this exception for an invalid index and abs() propagates it.
cases.description: Use a delegate that throws IndexOutOfBoundsException for negative indices (e.g., a ConstantIndicator that checks index). Calling abs().getValue(-1) must propagate the same exception.

cases.expected: RuntimeException (custom) when the delegate's getValue throws a user‑defined unchecked exception and abs() does not swallow it.
cases.description: Implement a delegate whose getValue method throws a custom RuntimeException (e.g., new RuntimeException("delegate failure")). Verify that abs().getValue(0) re‑throws the same exception.
